chapter_name: Through the Eyes of Travellers: Perceptions of Society
learning_objective: 🌍 See medieval India through the fascinating, highly distinct travelogues of Al-Biruni, Ibn Battuta, and François Bernier!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Coming from Uzbekistan (11th century), Al-Biruni wrote objectively about Indian religion, philosophy, and astronomy. He struggled to understand the caste system and completely rejected the notion of 'pollution' (untouchability), arguing that nature always cleanses itself.

A Moroccan traveler (14th century) who loved exploring. He was fascinated by things unfamiliar to him, like coconuts and paan (betel leaves). He was particularly amazed by the efficiency of the Indian postal system (Uluq and Dawa), which allowed merchants to send goods rapidly.

A French doctor (17th century) who constantly compared Mughal India unfavorably to Europe. He wrongly claimed that the Mughal Emperor owned all the land (preventing a strong middle class) and described Mughal cities as mere 'camp towns' that collapsed when the king moved.

Travellers often noted the conditions of women. Ibn Battuta wrote about female slaves acting as spies for the Sultan. Bernier provided a horrifying and detailed description of the practice of Sati, emphasizing the coercion involved.
Al-Biruni noted three barriers to understanding India: Language (Sanskrit was difficult), differences in religious beliefs, and the insularity (self-absorption) of the local population.

fun_activity.title: 🥥 The 'Alien' Coconut
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine seeing a coconut for the very first time! Ibn Battuta described it as looking like a human head—with the fiber looking like hair and the two spots looking like eyes. Try describing an everyday object as if you are an alien seeing it for the first time!

exam_tips: 📌 Always contrast the three travelers: Al-Biruni was scholarly, Ibn Battuta was an adventurous explorer, and Bernier was a harsh European critic.
📌 Bernier’s concept of 'Crown ownership of land' is a favorite exam question. Explain how he believed it led to the ruin of agriculture.
📌 Detail the two types of postal systems described by Ibn Battuta: the horse post (Uluq) and the foot post (Dawa).
quick_recap: ⭐ Al-Biruni came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni.
⭐ Ibn Battuta was appointed as the Qazi (judge) of Delhi by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
⭐ François Bernier's book was titled 'Travels in the Mughal Empire'.
